teams.heading: Fiji concede 351 points across their last 11 test matches
teams.body: The Fiji senior men's side have scored 314 points across their last 11 games. Over that same 11-game period, they conceded 351 points. This results in an average of 28.5 points scored per game, alongside an average of 31.9 points conceded per match. Their biggest win in this 11-game window was a 63-10 home victory against Canada in September 2025 during the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage.

teams.heading: Will Joseph presses England claims following standout Gloucester victory over Harlequins
teams.body: Gloucester centre Will Joseph has strengthened his case for international honours after an impressive display in Saturday’s 48-0 Premiership victory over Harlequins. Joseph was central to a rampant Gloucester backline, crossing for one of his side's eight tries in a dominant performance at Kingsholm. While the result leaves Harlequins winless after two rounds, the form of the young English centre has provided a timely boost for his prospects ahead of the upcoming international window.

teams.heading: France prepares to face Fiji following previous victory last November
teams.body: France returns to action against Fiji in Round 4, looking to build on a current log position of 3rd place. In their last meeting, which took place in November 2025 during the International Friendlies, France secured a 34-21 victory over Fiji on home soil. Les Bleus head into this fixture with 2 wins and 1 loss from their 3 matches in the current Nations Championship, having scored 116 points and conceded 75 for a points difference of +41.

teams.heading: Ireland women seal seven-try victory over Japan in Cork test
teams.body: The Ireland women’s side secured a comprehensive 43-19 win against Japan at Virgin Media Park on Saturday. After an early deficit, Scott Bemand’s team responded with four first-half tries before pulling away after the interval. Beibhinn Parsons extended her all-time international try-scoring record to 25, while Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett marked their respective debuts with second-half scores. The victory follows a win against the same opponents in Galway last week, providing momentum ahead of the upcoming WXV series.

teams.body: As the squad prepares for their upcoming fixture against South Africa, they look back on their progression in the international rankings. Following a challenging opening series in the 2026 Nations Championship, the team now aims to build on that historical benchmark during their November test matches in Turin, Genoa, and Udine.

teams.heading: Scotland women’s side suffer heavy home defeat against visiting Australia
teams.body: The Scotland women's side were defeated 30-10 by Australia in their WXV Global Series match at Hive Stadium. Despite leading 10-5 at half-time through an Evie Gallagher try and points from Helen Nelson, Scotland conceded 25 unanswered points in the second half. The match saw Scotland's Gallagher receive a 10-minute sin-bin during a pivotal eight-minute period where the Wallaroos scored three tries to secure their first victory of the season.

teams.heading: Josh Adams eyes Australia return as Wales winger targets third World Cup
teams.body: Wales wing Josh Adams has confirmed he is back in training and targeting a return to action this month after missing the July tour with a calf injury. The 31-year-old, who has 72 caps, is looking to reach his third global tournament and remains eager to feature in next year's competition in Australia. As Wales begin their countdown to the opening pool match against Zimbabwe, Adams is prioritising a healthy return to domestic play to secure his spot in future international squads.

teams.heading: Hunter Paisami suspended for four matches following dangerous tackle incident
teams.body: Wallabies centre Hunter Paisami has been ruled out of the upcoming Bledisloe Cup series after failing to overturn a four-match suspension. Paisami was cited for a dangerous tackle on Springboks fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu during the recent victory in Perth. Following a hearing, the disciplinary committee determined the action warranted a six-match entry point, reduced to four due to mitigating factors. Consequently, Les Kiss has called up Queensland Reds full-back Jock Campbell to the squad to bolster the backline options.

lead.why: Hunter Paisami's confirmed four-match ban is a significant personnel change ahead of the upcoming Tests against New Zealand.

teams.heading: Japan women's side fall to seven-try defeat against Ireland away
teams.body: The Japan women's side concluded their latest tour with a 43-19 defeat to Ireland at Virgin Media Park in Cork on Saturday. Despite an early try from Sakurako Korai, the Sakura XV struggled to contain the Irish attack, conceding seven tries throughout the contest. Nami Asari and Nijiho Nagata also crossed the whitewash for the visitors, but Ireland maintained control to secure consecutive victories. This result follows their earlier narrow defeat in the WXV Global Series encounter in Galway.

lead.why: The Japan women's national team match against Ireland is the most prominent event in the current reporting cycle, despite the app's default focus on the men's game.

teams.heading: Stormers lament missed opportunities following Edinburgh defeat and Andre-Hugo Venter injury blow
teams.body: John Dobson's Stormers side suffered a 17-13 defeat against Edinburgh at Hive Stadium on Friday evening, compounded by a first-half injury to hooker Andre-Hugo Venter. Venter was forced off the pitch in the 22nd minute after failing a head injury assessment following a friendly-fire head clash, severely disrupting the visitors' lineout execution as they managed to win only 57% of their 21 throws. Despite briefly holding a 13-10 lead through a Hacjivah Dayimani try, the Cape side were ultimately undone in the Scottish capital.
